stem: A client develops sudden severe leg pain with pallor, coolness, and absent distal pulses. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: These findings are most consistent with a benign positional circulation change that can be observed until warmth and pulses return without urgent evaluation.
options.B: These findings suggest acute limb ischemia, a vascular emergency requiring rapid recognition and emergency evaluation to preserve limb viability.
options.C: These findings are most consistent with an uncomplicated muscle strain because acute musculoskeletal pain commonly causes pallor and loss of distal pulses.
options.D: These findings indicate chronic venous insufficiency because venous disease typically causes sudden pulselessness, coolness, and severe ischemic pain.

rationale: The 2024 ACC/AHA multisociety PAD guideline defines acute limb ischemia as acute limb hypoperfusion characterized by findings that can include pain, pallor, pulselessness, and poikilothermia/coolness. Section 11 calls ALI a vascular emergency requiring rapid recognition and emergency evaluation. B therefore fits the presentation and urgency. A delays care despite ischemic signs, C cannot explain pallor and absent pulses as a simple strain, and D misclassifies an acute arterial emergency as chronic venous disease.
educational_objective: Recognize sudden pain, pallor, coolness, and pulselessness as acute limb ischemia requiring emergency vascular evaluation.
source_organization: American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association and multisociety writing committee
source_document_title: 2024 Guideline for the Management of Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease
source_locator: Table 2 Definitions of PAD Key Terms — ALI; Section 11 Acute Limb Ischemia; §11.1 Initial Clinical Evaluation and Diagnostic Approach to ALI.
source_claim_supported: ALI may present with pain, pallor, pulselessness and poikilothermia/coolness and is a vascular emergency requiring rapid recognition and emergency assessment to maximize limb salvage.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

source_original.stem: A client develops sudden severe leg pain with pallor, coolness, and absent distal pulses. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: These findings are most consistent with a benign positional circulation change that can be observed until warmth and pulses return without urgent evaluation.
options.B: These findings suggest acute limb ischemia, a vascular emergency requiring rapid recognition and urgent evaluation to preserve tissue and limb viability.
options.C: These findings are most consistent with an uncomplicated muscle strain because acute musculoskeletal pain commonly causes pallor and loss of distal pulses.
options.D: These findings indicate chronic venous insufficiency because venous disease typically causes sudden pulselessness, coolness, and severe ischemic pain.

source_original.rationale: The sudden combination of severe pain, pallor, coolness, and absent pulses is characteristic of acute limb ischemia, which the 2024 multisociety guideline describes as a vascular emergency. Option B correctly identifies the condition and urgency. Option A incorrectly treats ischemic signs as a benign positional change. Option C cannot explain pallor and absent pulses as a simple muscle strain. Option D misclassifies an acute arterial emergency as chronic venous disease.
source_original.source_detail: 2024 AHA/ACC Multisociety Guideline for Lower Extremity PAD — Acute Limb Ischemia: acute hypoperfusion presents with findings including pain, pallor, pulselessness and poikilothermia/coolness and is a vascular emergency requiring rapid recognition and emergency evaluation. 2024 multisociety PAD guideline remains current; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, medical emergencies and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained key and construct. Tightened urgency wording to the guideline's explicit 'vascular emergency' and 'emergency basis' language and avoided adding a tissue-viability time threshold not needed in the item.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Signs and emergency status are directly guideline-supported; no unnecessary anticoagulation or revascularization specifics added.

distractor_audit.A: Unsafe delay despite classic acute ischemia.
distractor_audit.C: Muscle strain does not account for absent pulses/pallor.
distractor_audit.D: Chronic venous disease does not explain this acute arterial pattern.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B fits all findings and urgency.
audit_findings.cueing: Parallel diagnostic interpretations; no second answer.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Verified exact ALI definition and emergency-evaluation text against the full guideline.
